location: Chapter 1.7, Convent of Caripe; Cavern of the Guacharo
location_zh: 第 1 卷第 7 章《卡里佩修道院；瓜查罗洞》
text_en: The natives connect mystic ideas with this cave, inhabited by nocturnal birds; they believe that the souls of their ancestors sojourn in the deep recesses of the cavern. "Man," say they, "should avoid places which are enlightened neither by the sun (zis), nor by the moon (nuna)." 'To go and join the guacharos,' is with them a phrase signifying to rejoin their fathers, to die.
text_zh: 当地人把这个洞和种种神秘的观念联系在一起；他们相信，祖先的灵魂就住在洞的深处。他们说：“人应该避开太阳（zis）和月亮（nuna）都照不到的地方。”“去和瓜查罗鸟做伴”，在他们的话里意思就是去和祖先团聚，也就是死去。

location: Chapter 1.7, Convent of Caripe; Cavern of the Guacharo
location_zh: 第 1 卷第 7 章《卡里佩修道院；瓜查罗洞》
text_en: Darkness is everywhere connected with the idea of death. The Grotto of Caripe is the Tartarus of the Greeks; and the guacharos, which hover over the rivulet, uttering plaintive cries, remind us of the Stygian birds.
text_zh: 黑暗在哪里都和死亡的观念联系在一起。卡里佩洞就是希腊人的塔耳塔罗斯；那些在溪流上空盘旋、发出哀鸣的瓜查罗鸟，叫人想起冥河边的鸟。

text_en: When we were come to the tops of the first hills of the plains adjoining to the river, we beheld that wonderful breach of waters which ran down Caroli; and might from that mountain see the river how it ran in three parts, above twenty miles off, and there appeared some ten or twelve overfalls in sight, every one as high over the other as a church tower, which fell with that fury, that the rebound of water made it seem as if it had been all covered over with a great shower of rain; and in some places we took it at the first for a smoke that had risen over some great town.
highlight_en: that wonderful breach of waters which ran down Caroli
text_zh: 当我们登上河边平原最前面那几座小山的山顶，就看见了卡罗尼河上那奇妙的大水奔泻；从那座山上能望见河水分成三股，在二十多英里外流着，眼前出现了十来道瀑布，一道比一道高，每道都有教堂塔楼那么高，水势凶猛，溅起的水花让整片地方看上去像下着一场大雨；有些地方我们起初还以为是哪座大城上空升起的烟。
highlight_zh: 卡罗尼河上那奇妙的大水奔泻

text_en: I never saw a more beautiful country, nor more lively prospects; hills so raised here and there over the valleys; the river winding into divers branches; the plains adjoining without bush or stubble, all fair green grass; the ground of hard sand, easy to march on, either for horse or foot; the deer crossing in every path; the birds towards the evening singing on every tree with a thousand several tunes; cranes and herons of white, crimson, and carnation, perching in the river's side; the air fresh with a gentle easterly wind; and every stone that we stooped to take up promised either gold or silver by his complexion.
text_zh: 我从没见过更美的地方，更生机勃勃的景色：山丘在谷地间这里那里隆起；河流分成好几条支汊蜿蜒而去；旁边的平原没有灌木也没有残茬，全是青翠的好草；地是硬沙，人马走起来都很轻松；每条小路上都有鹿穿过；傍晚时每棵树上都有鸟用千百种调子歌唱；白色、深红、肉粉色的鹤和鹭栖在河边；空气清新，吹着和缓的东风；我们弯腰捡起的每一块石头，看颜色都像是含着金子或银子。

text_en: In 1891 the flood was so high that the stores and dwellings of the part of the city fronting the river were inundated to a height of several feet. Then the inhabitants were obliged to have recourse to canoes in passing from house to house. Then, too, stray alligators were seen in the streets and it was possible to catch enough fish for a meal in the patio--court-yard--of one's residence.
text_zh: 1891 年那场洪水涨得极高，城里临河那一带的商店和住宅都被淹了好几英尺深。居民只好划着独木舟从一家到另一家。那时街上还能看到走散的鳄鱼，在自家的院子里就能钓到够吃一顿的鱼。

location: Chapter 8, The Outlying Pickets of the New World
location_zh: 第 8 章《新世界的前哨》
text_en: When we had crossed the second ridge we saw before us an irregular, palm-studded plain, and then the line of high red cliffs which I have seen in the picture. There it lies, even as I write, and there can be no question that it is the same.
highlight_en: the line of high red cliffs
text_zh: 翻过第二道山梁，我们眼前是一片起伏不平、点缀着棕榈的平原，再往前就是我在那幅画里见过的那一线高高的红色悬崖。此刻我写这些字的时候，它就在那里，毫无疑问就是同一个地方。
highlight_zh: 那一线高高的红色悬崖
